summary: Discovery focused on model selection for embedded assistant and mission planning workflows. Customer evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private for latency, multilingual support (EN/JP/ES), long-context (32k+), and tool-calling (live telemetry/tooling). Key ask: recommended open models and quantization/latency tradeoffs plus benchmark plan.
topics: hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment
transcript: [00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. quick intro - i'm Samir AE on the Redwood team, with Jules our solutions engineer.
[00:05] Maya: Hi thanks, i'm Maya, head of ML at Oceanside. we build navigation and operator assistants for marine drones.
[00:12] Jules: great, can you give a little context on what you're trying to solve? we prepared a couple of notes around context size and multilingual needs.

[00:18] Maya: Sure - two main surfaces. one, operator chat assistant that needs long context, like 20-30k tokens because they paste logs and mission state. two, mission planning where we want tool calls to our flight control APIs and telemetry integrations. Also we have teams in japan and spain so japanese and spanish support matters.
[00:35] Luca: latency is important too - for operator assist we want sub-400ms token latencies ideally, but for planning flows we can tolerate higher.
[00:45] Jules: okay let me ask about throughput - how many concurrent sessions/requests are you seeing?
[00:48] Priya: Right now prototype is ~30 concurrent users with spike to 120 during active ops. target is 500 concurrent in year one.
[00:56] Samir: good, that helps sizing. regarding model selection - are you leaning open models or closed (OpenAI/Anthropic)?
[01:02] Maya: we prefer open models for cost and control. but we need tool-calling and good multilingual quality. do open models support function calling reliably?

[01:10] Jules: function calling/structured outputs vary by model and runtime. Redwood supports tool calling as a layer - we can map model outputs to your API, do robust schema enforcement, and fallback when the model hallucinate. but model choice affects reliability; some open models have weaker instruction-following or tokenization quirks in Japanese.
[01:30] Maya: what about context length - we might need 64k for full mission logs. are there open models that can handle that and still be performant?

[01:38] Jules: there are a few 32k models and emerging 64k variants. performance depends on quantization and GPU memory. for Dedicated we can provision larger GPU partitions and use KV cache optimizations. for Hosted we have model variants that are verified but 64k workloads may be better on Dedicated/Private for cost predictability.
[01:55] Luca: can you clarify cost delta between hosted and dedicated for high throughput long-context?

[02:00] Samir: typically hosted is cheapest for low volume prototyping. once you hit sustained throughput with large contexts, Dedicated reserved capacity reduces per-token cost because of fixed GPUs and better batching. we'll send a cost matrix.
[02:12] Maya: security - we need VPC, KMS for keys, SOC 2 + audit logs. can Redwood Private run on-prem? we have some air-gapped sites.

[02:20] Jules: yes, Redwood Private supports VPC and an on-prem package. KMS/HSM integrations are supported. we'll share our SOC2 docs and a checklist - but note Private adds operational overhead but gives you full control.
[02:34] Maya: good. can you talk about multilingual quality? japanese particularly has been poor in past models.

[02:40] Jules: sure - japanese quality varies. we have evaluation profiles for models across en/jp/es. for some Llama derivatives and Mosaic-style open models, JP tokenization and instruction tuning help. we'll include evaluation scores and suggest finetune or prompt-engineering for JP-heavy flows.
[02:55] Priya: about tool-calling - how do you prevent the model from executing unsafe commands? we run heavy ops.

[03:01] Jules: two layers - runtime policy enforcement and sandboxing of tool endpoints. we can provide a safe adapter that validates model output schema, checks allowed endpoints and rate-limits. also can run canary tests to detect drift.
[03:15] Maya: what's the typical latency for tool calls that first need to call external telemetry then return to model for a follow-up generation?

[03:22] Jules: depends - synchronous tool calls add round trip time. we often prefetch telemetry or do async tool calls with model contexts updated later. for sub-400ms token latency we rely on optimized kernels, batching, and sometimes shorter context windows for generate-time critical paths.
[03:38] Luca: any limitations around KV cache eviction and long-running sessions?

[03:42] Jules: we support persistent KV caches for session affinity; eviction policies configurable. with very long context like 64k, we use prefix caching and summarize older content to keep working set small.
[03:52] Maya: ok next - benchmarking. we want Redwood to run a benchmark comparing 32k vs 64k variants and an OpenAI baseline. can you do that?
[03:59] Samir: yes - Jules will run a 48-hour benchmark on Dedicated or Hosted depending on capacity. we'll need sample prompts and a representative traffic pattern.
[04:08] Maya: we'll share prompts today. also curious about quantization - how much does it hurt multilingual instruction following?
[04:14] Jules: int8/4-bit quantization often has small degradation on fluency but can be mitigated by quant-aware calibration and eval; we'll show per-model quantized vs fp32 results.
[04:25] Priya: final question - single tenancy vs multi-tenant for compliance?
[04:29] Samir: Dedicated is single-tenant capacity; Private is full tenant isolation. Hosted is multi-tenant; we can discuss VPC peering and additional controls.
[04:38] Maya: thanks. recap of next steps?

[04:40] Samir: we'll send model matrix and cost comparisons, share SOC2 and KMS docs, schedule benchmarks. Jules will own the benchmark; Maya will share prompts. I'll follow up with Dedicated pricing.
[04:50] Maya: great, thanks everyone.
[04:53] Samir: thanks, talk soon.
